results.title: Neuromorphic algorithms for brain implants: a review - Frontiers
results.content: # Neuromorphic algorithms for brain implants: a review. We discuss current algorithms and emerging neurocomputational models that, when implemented on neuromorphic hardware, could match or surpass traditional methods in efficiency. Neuromorphic Algorithms often incorporate phenomena like neuron spiking, synaptic plasticity, and network-level dynamics, aiming to replicate the brain’s style of processing. While some run on standard CPUs or GPUs, specialized neuromorphic chips—analog, digital, or mixed-signal—offer advantages for pattern recognition, sensory data analysis, and real-time learning by minimizing data-transfer bottlenecks (Kudithipudi et al., 2025; Schuman et al., 2022). Emerging and future applications include cognitive enhancement, brain-to-brain communication, neural rehabilitation such as rewiring neural pathways to restore function after stroke or brain injury (Baker et al., 2023; Chiappalone et al., 2022; Donati and Valle, 2024; Rao et al., 2014; Vakilipour and Fekrvand, 2024). For example, a neuromorphic chip in an implant might adjust stimulation patterns in real time as brain states fluctuate, minimizing power consumption and improving clinical outcomes (Chiappalone et al., 2022; Donati and Valle, 2024).
